title: Function-backed action integration test
description: Proves that a function-backed action (createOrderAndUpdateInventory) executes via the embedded Goja runtime, produces 2 edits (CREATE Order + MODIFY Product to decrement stock), and those edits flow through the executor -> publisher -> consumer -> Bleve pipeline correctly.

function.name: createOrderAndUpdateInventory
function.description: Takes productId and quantity, creates an Order and decrements Product.stock

scenarios.name: apply_function_action
scenarios.setup: Product PROD-001 seeded with stock=100 in Bleve

notes: The function source is stored in PostgreSQL (functions table) and retrieved by RID during dispatch.
GojaDispatcher wraps functions.Runtime and a FunctionLookup interface (satisfied by the OMS PG repo).
Edits are tagged with Source='user' by tagEditsAsUserSource so the US-021 user-edit-wins guard protects them from subsequent ingest overwrites.
Consumer.ApplyBatch is called directly (no NATS) to apply edits to Bleve in the integration test.
The handler passes ontology API name (not RID) to executor.Apply; ListActionTypes supports both via OR query.
